## Tours through Chivay: why the town is part of the itinerary

**[Chivay](/peru/place/chivay/) lies in the mountainous [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) area.** On journeys through southern Peru, it connects two busy days: the drive from [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) to the canyon and the morning departure for the viewpoint used to observe Andean condors. The itinerary usually continues afterwards to [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/).

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Every confirmed option includes Chivay within a larger Peru itinerary. When choosing, it is important to understand that the town is primarily **an overnight stop and starting point for exploring the Colca**, not a separate multi-day resort.

In each option, distinguish three experiences: a stop in town, the trip to canyon viewpoints and an **optional visit to hot springs**. They should not be assumed to form one automatically included service.

## Five itineraries through Chivay: key differences

All current journeys include Peru's cultural areas and the Andes, but they pursue different goals after the Colca section. Choose according to what you want to add to the country's main historical attractions.

| Itinerary | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| [Peru in 12 days](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/) | Classic southern Peru |
| [Peru and the Candelaria festival](/peru/tour/peru-inca-empire-candelaria-festival/) | 13 days, festival itinerary |
| [Peru with Trujillo and Chiclayo](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/) | 14 days, northern archaeology |
| [Peru and Iquitos](/peru/tour/complete-peru-iquitos-15-days/) | 15 days, Amazon extension |
| [Peru and Tumbes beaches](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) | 16 days, seaside relaxation |

### 12 days: a classic route through the Andes

The [12-day Peru tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/) combines [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the Sacred Valley, Lake Titicaca and Colca Canyon. Day 8 involves the journey from Puno towards the Colca and arrival in Chivay. After spending the night, travellers visit Cruz del Cóndor and continue to Arequipa.

This is a good option if you want to see the country's historic and natural regions without extra long sections in the north or the rainforest. It still involves several transfers and adjustment to high altitude.

### 13 days: Peruvian history and Candelaria

On the [13-day itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-inca-empire-candelaria-festival/), Chivay follows Puno and Lake Titicaca. The next day takes travellers to the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint and then to Arequipa. The wider programme explicitly includes the Candelaria festival and a ticket to the event.

**The festival element is a genuine distinction.** Check the departure dates against the festival calendar: simply passing through Chivay does not guarantee attendance at the celebration outside its scheduled period. The Colca geography is otherwise comparable with other tours.

### 14 days: Colca Canyon and northern Peru's archaeology

The [14-day tour featuring Trujillo and Chiclayo](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/) includes an overnight stop in Chivay on the same mountain section. After Arequipa, travellers return to Lima and head north towards [Trujillo](/peru/place/trujillo/), [Chan Chan](/peru/place/chan-chan/) and [Chiclayo](/peru/place/chiclayo/).

This suits travellers who want to explore the civilisations of the northern coast alongside Inca heritage and Colca's nature. It adds more historical sites, as well as a busier schedule with additional flights.

### 15 days: the Amazon after the Andes

The [Complete Peru and Iquitos itinerary](/peru/tour/complete-peru-iquitos-15-days/) combines the Andes' classic monuments with an extension to [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/). Chivay remains an overnight stop before the morning visit to the Colca viewpoints. After the southern section, the programme continues to an Amazon lodge and nature excursions.

Choose this option if you want to contrast Peru's mountains with tropical forest and river wildlife. The terms and excursions in Iquitos are covered by the tour's own description; they are not services offered in Chivay.

### 16 days: mountains followed by the beach

On the [Complete Peru and Tumbes Beaches tour](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/), the journey continues to the coast after Cusco, Lake Titicaca, the Colca and Arequipa. Its final section takes place in [Tumbes](/peru/place/tumbes/).

It suits travellers who want to finish several days at altitude with time beside the Pacific Ocean. Chivay is not a multi-day relaxation destination on this route either: arrival in the evening, an overnight stay and the next day's canyon excursion are scheduled.

## How the Chivay stop works

### Arriving from Puno and spending the night in the valley

On the confirmed itineraries, the day begins around [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The journey to the Colca crosses high-altitude areas, with the group reaching Chivay towards the end of the day.

Several programmes specifically mention **Colca Llacta 3-star hotel** or accommodation of a comparable category. This is a condition of those particular published itineraries, not every possible trip through the town.

After the drive, guests can visit hot springs if they wish. The visit is described as **optional**, so admission, a separate transfer or SPA treatments should not automatically be treated as included. Check the paid services and arrival time of the tour you choose.

### The next morning: Cruz del Cóndor

On the following day, the route heads towards the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint. Several of our programmes indicate a journey of **approximately 1.5 hours from Chivay**. Visitors see the canyon and, in suitable conditions, Andean condors using rising air currents.

The condor is a wild bird, and its appearance depends on wind, weather and natural behaviour. The itinerary includes a trip to the viewpoint but cannot guarantee a sighting of a particular number of condors.

After the nature section, the groups continue to [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/). This sequence links Lake Titicaca, the canyon and southern Peru's second major city without returning to Puno.

## Chivay and Colca Canyon: different stops on the journey

Chivay is a town where travellers can stay overnight, have dinner and visit hot springs if time permits. [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) is a large natural area with mountain slopes, terraces, villages and viewpoints.

| Place | What it adds to the journey |
|---|---|
| [Chivay](/peru/place/chivay/) | Overnight stay, town, hot springs |
| [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) | Mountain panoramas and nature route |
| Cruz del Cóndor | Condor watching when conditions allow |
| [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/) | Next urban stage |

If birdwatching is your priority, the time of the trip to the viewpoint and the opportunity to wait matter more than the duration of your stay in Chivay itself. If the hot springs appeal most, check separately whether your selected tour's schedule leaves time for them after the drive.

## Altitude, weather and preparing for the road

Chivay is in the Andes at an elevation above 3,000 metres. By the time they arrive, many travellers have spent several days in the highlands around Cusco and Puno, but individual responses to altitude differ. Physical exertion and wellbeing need to be considered throughout the mountain section.

Mornings at the canyon can be cool and windy. Warm clothing, sun protection and comfortable shoes are useful for a visit to Cruz del Cóndor. Road travel takes up a substantial part of the days, so assess the schedule as a whole: journey from Puno, overnight stay, morning stops and further travel to Arequipa.

Weather affects both canyon visibility and chances of observing condors. A nature-focused itinerary should allow for such variations rather than assuming the same conditions on every date.

## What to choose after Chivay

Chivay fits itineraries with quite different goals because each connects [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/). The differences emerge afterwards.

If you want to focus on **Cusco, Machu Picchu and southern Peru**, start with the [12-day tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/). An interest in northern coastal civilisations leads towards the [14-day Chiclayo itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/). For a contrast of natural environments, compare the journey including [Iquitos](/peru/tour/complete-peru-iquitos-15-days/) with the route to [Tumbes beaches](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/).

Other programmes in this region are available in the [Colca Canyon tours catalogue](/peru/place/colca-canyon/tour/), while all active trips in the country appear under [Peru tours](/peru/tour/). You can also explore [nature-focused Peru tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/peru/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Chivay

### How many nights do the tours spend in Chivay?

All five confirmed programmes include **one overnight stay** after the road journey from Puno. The following morning, travellers head to Cruz del Cóndor and then continue towards Arequipa.

### Are hot springs included in the price?

The tour descriptions list a visit to the hot springs as **optional**. That does not confirm inclusion of admission or transfers in the base fare. Check the conditions of the particular itinerary.

### Can you see condors?

The routes include a visit to the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint, where Andean condors can be observed. Sightings depend on natural conditions and cannot be guaranteed.

### Is it compulsory to visit Arequipa after Chivay?

All five current tours in this selection continue to Arequipa after the Colca section. A different sequence requires a separately arranged itinerary.

### Which tour should I choose if I want the ocean after the mountains?

The [16-day Tumbes beaches itinerary](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) continues to the Pacific coast after the sightseeing stage. If you would prefer rainforest over beaches, compare the [15-day Iquitos tour](/peru/tour/complete-peru-iquitos-15-days/).

## Colca Canyon: seeing condors and planning a trip from Arequipa

**Colca Canyon (Cañón del Colca) is one of [Peru's](/peru/) most spectacular natural regions.** The valley lies in Caylloma Province in the [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/) region. Steep slopes, ancient agricultural terraces and mountain communities create scenery quite unlike the city of Arequipa.

For many travellers, the main attraction is **watching Andean condors in flight** from the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint. But the canyon is rewarding even when no birds appear: the road passes mountains, valleys and terraces, while villages introduce the cultures of the Collagua and Cabana peoples.

## How to get there and where to stay

A common itinerary begins in Arequipa and heads towards **Chivay**. According to Peru Travel, the journey takes approximately **3–3.5 hours by car or bus**, with further travel needed to reach the canyon's main viewpoints. A one-day excursion therefore usually begins very early and involves a great deal of time on the road.

For a less hurried experience, spend a night in the valley. That allows you to visit different villages, rest after the high-altitude drive and head out to see condors in the morning without making the long transfer from Arequipa on the same day.

Altitude changes substantially along the way. **Chivay stands around 3,600 metres above sea level**, while high mountain passes may be higher. Consider your personal tolerance of altitude, drink enough water and avoid overly strenuous activity immediately after arriving from the coast.

## Cruz del Cóndor: why birds soar above the canyon

The **Cruz del Cóndor** viewpoint is known for opportunities to watch large birds riding rising air currents along the cliffs. The Andean condor can have a wingspan of up to **3 metres**; when one flies near the edge of the canyon, its size is striking even without special equipment.

Condors are free-ranging wild birds, so sightings cannot be guaranteed. Visits are generally arranged in the morning, but their success depends on weather, wind and the birds' behaviour. Binoculars and a camera lens suitable for shooting from a distance are helpful.

Observe barriers at the viewpoints and do not approach cliff edges just to take photographs. The panoramic canyon remains impressive whether or not a condor passes during your stop.

## Terraces, villages and other experiences in the valley

Colca has a long agricultural history. Its slopes are covered with **andenes**, stepped terraces where local communities have grown crops for centuries despite the difficult mountain terrain. Around Chivay, Yanque and Coporaque, travellers can discover handicrafts and everyday life.

There are several ways to experience the region:

| Format | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Viewpoints | Panoramas and condors |
| Valley villages | Traditions and terraces |
| Hot springs | Relaxation near Chivay |
| Extended trekking | Descending into and climbing out of the canyon |

**A sightseeing excursion and a trek to the canyon floor differ significantly in difficulty.** Descending on foot to great depth takes time, suitable shoes and physical fitness; the climb back out can be much harder than a walk between viewpoints.

## When to visit Colca

The region has pronounced seasonal changes, with rapid temperature shifts at altitude. Stable weather makes walking and photography more comfortable; trails and roads can be less predictable during the rainy season.

Even on sunny days, bring a warm layer, windproof clothing and sun protection. Avoid scheduling another demanding activity immediately after returning to Arequipa from a high-altitude excursion. Admission arrangements, fees and access to specific trails follow local rules and should be checked before visiting.

**Colca and the Andagua Volcanoes** received **UNESCO Global Geopark status in 2019**. This recognises the region's geological heritage and should not be confused with inscription on the World Heritage List.

## Colca on Ada Tours itineraries

The canyon is part of our [21-day journey through Peru](/peru/tour/best-of-peru-21-days/). Another [tour through Lima, Cusco, Titicaca, Colca and Arequipa](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/) combines Andean attractions with historic cities.

Compare the number of nights in the valley, time allowed at Cruz del Cóndor and difficulty of the walks. The word "Colca" in a tour name does not itself mean that a descent into the canyon or guaranteed condor sightings are included.

## Frequently asked questions about Colca Canyon

### Can you see condors in Colca?

Yes. Cruz del Cóndor is known for observing these birds, although sightings depend on natural conditions.

### How long is the journey from Arequipa to Colca?

Allow approximately 3–3.5 hours to Chivay and extra travel time to the viewpoints.

### Is an overnight stay in the valley necessary?

An early departure from Arequipa is possible on a short sightseeing tour, but staying overnight provides more time and reduces the rush.

### Is Colca worthwhile without trekking?

Yes. Panoramic views, agricultural terraces and viewpoints can be enjoyed on a sightseeing excursion without long hikes.

## How to choose a tour through Colca Canyon

Travellers visit [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) for its mountain scenery, terraced slopes and the chance to see Andean condors. When choosing a tour, however, it is more helpful to compare **the daily itinerary and direction of travel than the canyon's overall depth**. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Colca on the main itinerary. These programmes vary in duration, but **extra days do not necessarily mean more time in the canyon itself**. They may instead be devoted to the Amazon, the coast or monuments in northern Peru.

## How Colca is visited on Ada Tours itineraries

Several routes include a transfer from Puno to the Colca area after visits to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lake Titicaca. The road passes mountain plateaus, viewpoints and Lake Lagunillas, where waterbirds can be observed. The group reaches Chivay in the evening. This town is a convenient base for the canyon's panoramic viewpoints.

The following morning is devoted to Cruz del Cóndor. On the selected itineraries, travellers visit the viewpoint before continuing to Arequipa. A separate drive is needed from Chivay, and **arriving at the viewpoint is not the same as seeing a condor**. The birds fly freely; their appearance and distance from observers depend on natural conditions.

The [Classic Peru tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/), [Peru and Iquitos](/peru/tour/complete-peru-iquitos-15-days/) and [Peru and Tumbes beaches](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) programmes also mention an optional visit to Chivay's hot springs. It is described as an activity available on request and should not automatically be treated as paid for in every tour.

### How a sightseeing stop differs from trekking

**The presence of Colca on an itinerary does not mean a hike to the canyon floor is included.** The journeys described above mainly involve road transfers, panoramic stops and condor watching. If you want a multi-day descent on foot, overnight stays along the trail and the climb back out, the physical demands and a separate itinerary must be discussed specifically. A guided trek cannot be inferred from the word "canyon" in a tour title.

## Which Colca itinerary is best for you?

### A first introduction to southern Peru

The [12-day journey through Lima, Cusco, Titicaca, Colca and Arequipa](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/) offers a coherent introduction to the south. Cities and Inca heritage come first, followed by the high-altitude lake, the road to the canyon and Arequipa's architecture. In the programme description, [Paracas and the Nazca Lines](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) are listed as possible additions rather than guaranteed included days.

### Andean nature plus Amazon rainforest

The [15-day itinerary including Iquitos](/peru/tour/complete-peru-iquitos-15-days/) retains the Peruvian mountain section and continues to [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/). The Amazon stage differs from Colca in both climate and logistics: it is a separate region with boat outings and a nature programme. Choose it if you want to experience the highlands as well as humid tropical forest, allowing for the extra flight and travel days.

### Northern archaeology after the Andes

On the [14-day tour through Trujillo and Chiclayo](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/), the historical journey continues after Colca and Arequipa. [Trujillo](/peru/place/trujillo/) and [Chiclayo](/peru/place/chiclayo/) introduce cultures that developed beyond the core of the Inca Empire. This suits travellers who prefer a variety of archaeological sites to beach relaxation.

### Seaside relaxation after the highlands

The [16-day Tumbes beaches tour](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) combines sightseeing with several days on the Pacific coast. The beach section follows the main Andean trips, separating leisure time from the longer days of excursions. Flights, accommodation and meals for this option are detailed in the tour's own programme.

### A festival itinerary or the longest journey

The [13-day Candelaria festival tour](/peru/tour/peru-inca-empire-candelaria-festival/) has a clearly defined event focus. It suits travellers who choose their dates around a cultural celebration in Puno rather than only visiting the usual sights.

The [21-day Peru journey](/peru/tour/best-of-peru-21-days/) covers a wider range of places and includes additional days in other regions. When comparing it with shorter tours, consider how much time is devoted to transport, walking and rest.

## Arranging the drive through Chivay and Cruz del Cóndor

The main points for planning are [Chivay](/peru/place/chivay/), Colca's viewpoints and the onward road to Arequipa. Peru's official tourism portal gives an approximate distance of 151 km and a driving time of about three hours from Arequipa to Chivay, followed by another 42 km or so to Cruz del Cóndor. On a private itinerary, actual travel time depends on stops, road conditions and the route.

If the journey runs **from Puno to Colca**, the day is quite different from a standard return trip from Arequipa. When comparing itineraries, simply finding the name "Arequipa" is therefore not enough: check where the drive begins, where the overnight stay is scheduled and which day includes the condor viewpoint.

Altitude affects people differently. A sudden ascent after flying in from the coast can be more challenging than a gradual journey through the mountains. On programmes passing through Cusco and Puno, high-altitude stages follow one another, but individual reactions to altitude are not determined by how busy the sightseeing programme is. If you are prone to altitude sickness, discuss pacing and health concerns with a doctor in advance.

## When to go and what to pack

Peruvian tourism recommendations often favour mornings for condor watching. But this is **wildlife observation, not a scheduled demonstration**: a close flypast cannot be promised. Cold mornings, strong sunlight and substantial temperature changes during the day are all possible in the mountain valley. Bring a warm layer, sun protection, water and comfortable footwear.

Choose dates with the entire itinerary in mind: rainy periods in the Andes, access to mountain roads and the season on the coast or in the Amazon differ. The question "When is Colca best?" does not determine the season for a whole multi-region journey. Check the sequence of days, especially if you want to combine the canyon with [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and the beaches.

## Frequently asked questions about Colca tours

### How many days does a tour spend in the canyon itself?

On many programmes, the main Colca stage consists of a transfer and an overnight stay around Chivay, followed by Cruz del Cóndor before the drive to Arequipa. A total tour length of 12, 15 or 21 days does not itself indicate how many hours will be spent at the canyon. Read the individual daily programme.

### Are condor sightings guaranteed?

No. Cruz del Cóndor is a place to observe wild birds. The viewpoint is included on the confirmed itineraries, but sightings and how closely birds fly depend on weather and their behaviour.

### Are Chivay's hot springs included in the price?

Several programmes offer the hot springs **as an option**. This does not confirm that admission is automatically included. The "Included" section of each tour determines which services are paid for.

### Can Colca and Machu Picchu be combined?

Yes. All the Peru itineraries listed above that feature Colca also include [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The transfers between regions take place on different days. Compare options in the [general Peru tours catalogue](/peru/tour/).

### Can trekking through the canyon be added?

Such a trip requires separate agreement on the route, duration, physical requirements and overnight stays. Including Colca on a sightseeing tour does not establish that a descent on foot is part of the package.

### Should I choose Colca or more days in Cusco?

If you are particularly interested in high-altitude valley scenery and condor watching, keep Colca in the itinerary. For a deeper introduction to Inca architecture, extra days in [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/) may be more rewarding. With a short holiday, this is a better criterion than trying to fit every stop into one journey.

## Coricancha in Cusco: the Temple of the Sun beneath Santo Domingo Convent

**Coricancha** is one of the best-known sanctuaries of ancient [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). At the height of the Inca state, it was associated with sun worship, important rituals and the religious life of the capital. After the Spanish conquest, Santo Domingo Convent was built over part of the complex.

Visitors now see two architectural traditions at once: precisely fitted stone blocks from the Inca foundations and the walls of the later Christian monastic complex. This contrast offers a deeper understanding of Cusco's history than an ordinary walk through the central squares.

## Inca stonework and the structure of the sanctuary

Coricancha's surviving walls demonstrate exceptional skill in shaping and joining stone blocks. Stones were fitted with great precision, while the layout of rooms was connected with religious purposes. Historical accounts identify Coricancha as a centre of worship of the Sun and other important forces in the Inca worldview.

Pre-Hispanic architecture remains visible in the foundations and individual walls. The functions of the site changed after the colonial convent was built, but the earlier structures did not disappear entirely. UNESCO highlights this continuity in the urban fabric when describing historic Cusco.

Allow time to examine the masonry and interior spaces. Particular rooms may have their own admission rules, and reconstructed sections should be distinguished from the original archaeological fabric.

## Santo Domingo: colonial architecture over an earlier city

The Santo Domingo convent complex developed after the Spanish conquest of Peru. Its construction on the site of Coricancha clearly illustrates how Spanish religious buildings were erected over some of the Inca capital's most important centres.

For anyone interested in religious history and architecture, this visit differs from seeing ruins in the open air. Here the interiors of a Christian convent can be compared directly with the techniques used to build Inca walls. That is one reason Coricancha often features in historical city tours.

## Buying tickets and planning the visit

Cusco has a tourist ticket known as the **Boleto Turístico del Cusco**, covering several groups of museums and archaeological sites. The official COSITUC organisation separately includes **the museum at Coricancha** in its city ticket package. Admission to the museum and entry to the monastic complex itself may, however, be governed by different arrangements.

Before visiting, check which part of the complex you intend to see and precisely what the ticket covers. Buying a ticket for archaeological sites outside the city does not automatically provide access to every convent in Cusco. Check opening hours for your travel date as well.

## Coricancha and archaeological sites around Cusco

After the Temple of the Sun, you can continue towards [Sacsayhuamán](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/), [Qenqo](/peru/place/qenqo/), [Puka Pukara](/peru/place/puka-pukara/) and [Tambomachay](/peru/place/tambomachay/). These are separate archaeological sites with different locations and purposes.

**Qenqo** is known for passages and niches carved into rock. **Puka Pukara** has stone walls and open terraces above the road. **Tambomachay** is associated with a stone water-channel system. Coricancha in the city centre and the outlying complexes can be combined in a single sightseeing day, but time must be allowed for transport and admission.

## Frequently asked questions about Coricancha

### Are Coricancha and Santo Domingo the same building?

They are parts of one historic ensemble: an Inca sanctuary and later monastic architecture occupy connected areas. Their different origins and functions should be recognised when visiting.

### Can you visit Coricancha independently?

Visiting arrangements depend on the complex's rules. Independent visits are possible in areas open to visitors, but guided explanations help provide a deeper understanding of Inca history.

### Is the Boleto Turístico required?

The Cusco tourist ticket covers certain museums and attractions, including the Coricancha museum. Access to the complex itself should be checked separately under the current arrangements.

### Is it part of Machu Picchu?

No. Coricancha is in [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), while [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is a separate mountain citadel. Both are connected with Inca history but require different travel arrangements.

## What else is usually visited in Cusco with Coricancha?

Several programmes visit four other archaeological sites after Coricancha. They help show how Inca religious and defensive architecture extended beyond the city itself.

- [Sacsayhuamán](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/) is known for enormous, precisely fitted stone blocks and its elevated position above Cusco.
- [Qenqo](/peru/place/qenqo/) is associated with ritual architecture, including passages and features carved directly into rock.
- [Puka Pukara](/peru/place/puka-pukara/) has another kind of stone structures, traditionally associated with control of a road and defence.
- [Tambomachay](/peru/place/tambomachay/) is known for its stone waterworks.

## Combining Coricancha, Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley

[Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is a convenient base for discovering Inca heritage. In the city, you can see Coricancha, squares, colonial facades and preserved Inca foundations beneath buildings. The [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) reveals another aspect of this history: ancient settlements, agricultural terraces and the Urubamba Valley. [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/) combines architecture with the railway logistics for reaching [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

If your main interest is the temple and its nearest monuments, a city sightseeing day may be enough. To explore Inca history more deeply, seek out programmes with separate days for the valley and Machu Picchu. These matter more than the overall length of a multi-country journey that may allocate only part of its schedule to Peru.

Historic Cusco lies at approximately 3,400 metres above sea level, as noted in UNESCO materials. Allow time to adjust to the altitude after arrival, particularly before a busy excursion and subsequent mountain travel. Opening dates and ticket conditions depend on the chosen trip and must be checked before visiting.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Coricancha

### Is Coricancha a separate full-day excursion?

On the programmes covered here, Coricancha is normally part of a wider sightseeing day in and around Cusco. The exact timing is set out in each itinerary. Listing the Temple of the Sun does not mean a full day is dedicated to it alone.

### Are the Temple of the Sun and Santo Domingo Convent at different addresses?

The complex occupies one historic site: part of the Inca structures survive beneath the later monastic architecture. This juxtaposition makes the visit valuable. More historical details appear on the [Coricancha page](/peru/place/coricancha/).

### Is Coricancha included on a trip to Uyuni?

Yes. The temple is part of the Cusco sightseeing day on the [12-day Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) and also features on the [15-day version with Altiplano lakes](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/).

### Can I choose a journey including Coricancha without visiting five countries?

Yes. There is a [10-day Peru–Bolivia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/) and longer trips covering two or three countries. You do not have to book a five-country tour to see the Temple of the Sun.

### Do all programmes include admission tickets and Russian-speaking guides?

There is no basis for making that blanket claim. Some programmes explicitly specify a Russian-speaking guide on a particular day; admission tickets and guiding languages must be checked for each itinerary separately. Sharing the name of an attraction does not mean the terms are the same.

First check the dates and principal event: an ordinary journey, New Year, Carnival or the Champions' Parade. Then compare group versus private format, country order and the complete list of inclusions.
